applied.change: The class ladder is now read, not transcribed. `LADDER = ("f-", "b-", "i-", "cli-")` is deleted; `run.ladder(gi)` sorts `gi.ROUTING_TABLE` - the same table harness/gateway/routing.json gives the gateway to route on - by its recorded `unit_micros_per_1k` at call time, so no prefix is written down anywhere in the example. `step_class` takes the rungs as an argument and returns the current class unchanged when either the current or the declared class is not in the table, instead of raising ValueError on `LADDER.index(None)`. The extension-points row now says what is true: reprice or add a class in routing.json and the ladder moves. New visible check (step 5) asserts the ladder is the routing table in price order and the same length, that the top rung does not step past itself, and that a class the table does not carry is not stepped.

The fleet cell count now says what is measured. README's fleet row and provenance's measured line read '50 units x 2 attempts = 100 attempt cells and 100 measure cells, 200 distinct cell ids and no id reused', replacing 'one hundred distinct cells (one attempt cell and one measure cell each)', which only held if every unit finished in one attempt. test.sh step 11 now counts the measure cells as well as the attempt cells, asserts 200 distinct ids across both, and asserts the two sets do not overlap; its check label carries the same four numbers.

The class-step bound now lives on the document. `unit()` reads `escalation.class_steps_permitted` into `permitted` and gates on `steps_taken < permitted` in place of the hardcoded `not stepped` flag; a step that would not move the class (the ladder has no higher rung) is neither counted nor ledgered, so an `escalated` record now always means the class moved. The other escalation fields are read rather than decorative: the `escalated` record carries `esc["policy"]` and `esc["trigger"]` where the trigger sentence used to be a literal in the runner, and `approval-parked.asks` is now `esc["on_ceiling"]`. `template`, `form` and `source_ref` are carried onto the `unit-submitted` record with the attempt ceiling and the permit, so the declaration's identity fields are read somewhere. New visible check (step 5) runs the same unit at `class_steps_permitted` 0 and 1: 0 gives no escalated record and one model class across all three attempts, 1 gives exactly one step and two classes, and the record's trigger text equals the declaration's.

The 'On a refusal' row is split in two. 'On a refusal that ends the unit' names only the two that exist and are measured - document-invalid (422) and budget-exhausted (402), problem+json on stdout, exit 2. 'On a refusal taken inside the unit' says that a refused tool call never reaches the caller as a problem body and does not end the unit: it is folded into the capability-call record's refused list by its deciding rule id (declared-surface, read-only-verdict, both measured at step 10), that the second isolation class answers an unserved snapshot operation the same way with isolation-operation-unsupported (501) at step 9, and that an unregistered suffix is recorded as gap 1 rather than minted. The invented policy-denied (403) and isolation-unavailable (503) claims are gone.

test.sh gates on the count as well as on the failures: `FLOOR=45` at the top and `[ "$PASS" -ge "$FLOOR" ] || { echo ...; exit 1; }` beside the existing FAIL gate. Verified by construction: a copy of the file's first 20 lines plus the gate prints 'passed 0, failed 0', reports 'the visible check counted 0, below the floor of 45' and exits 1. The header cites F-a7-03 for why. provenance.visible_checks_counted moved 46 -> 50 in step with it.

provenance.cites is now exactly the 37 record ids the example's rows carry, checked by grepping every id out of README.md, the .py files, test.sh, units/ and contract/. X-litmus-d-006 (quoted at README gap 9) and F-a7-03 (now cited in test.sh's header) and X-unit-design-013 (cited in contract/tools.json) are in; the 24 ids that appear nowhere in the example are out. The REF- reading rows are kept because they name files the example actually reads. The wider reading list is not preserved elsewhere: the example-provenance shape is additionalProperties false, so there is no member to put it in. The file still validates against that shape with the reference example's validator (0 errors).

The adapters table's last column is renamed 'Second adapter on file, its execution model, and where it is proved', and the three 'as above' cells are replaced by each adapter's own execution model, taken from its own header: model access is a provider's asynchronous batch route (submit returns a ticket, claim polls, cost committed at submit and reconciled at claim, nothing cancellable once submitted); tool access is a catalogue authored and versioned outside this platform on a remote server holding its own authorization, re-read at every bind, cancel recorded not honoured; capability packaging is a registry loader resolving a namespace-scoped identity to a content digest and verifying it before anything is read. Each row now says where it is proved - containment here at step 9, the other three in their own harness gates. The errors row says it has no second implementation to swap.

The fan-out is read from the envelope the door sent: `fleet_size = args.fleet or envelope["payload"].get("fleet_size", 1)`, and the fleet path is taken when that width is above one, so `--fleet` is an override rather than the thing that fans out. The schedule door's command line in README section 3 and in the run-steps table loses `--fleet 50`; its 'What is different' cell now says payload.fleet_size 50 is what fans it out, and says plainly that payload.recurrence is carried and not consumed here because recurrence belongs to the scheduling capability the progress area exercises. test.sh step 11 runs the schedule door with no flag and gets fifty units, asserts the two documents' declared widths, and asserts `--fleet 4` overrides to four; step 1 narrows that one door to `--fleet 1` with a comment, because the door-convergence check compares the four doors unit for unit.

The extension-points table gains the evidence column the other five tables carry. Two rows are now cited and measured rather than asserted (containment class -> F-b1-02 plus step 9; class ladder -> F-a4-01 plus the new step 5 ladder check; attempt policy -> unit-design#escalation plus the new step 5 permit check), and the two that are this example's own conventions - the opaque criterion handle and the manifest-instead-of-listing contract - are marked proposed with their reasoning.

Recorded as a gap rather than claimed. The containment interface publishes admit, terminate, snapshot (pause/resume/fork) and one prompt turn, and no operation that runs a host-supplied check inside a cell, so the check bodies cannot be driven through the measure cell handle without a new interface operation - which is the gap. New README gap 10 states that the measure cell is admitted, ledgered and terminated while the check bodies run host-side against the candidate on the host filesystem, so the anti-tamper wording section 1 quotes is claimed here, not measured; its research query asks what operation an isolation interface should publish and what the grader returns through. The check-report ledger record now carries `checks_ran: "host-side"` so the claim is on the receipt rather than left to be assumed, test.sh step 11 asserts it on all 100 measure records, and provenance moves the tamper-proof line into claimed.
